summary: The existing collective-possibility dossier and Third Way declarations distinguish the contested shift from temporal plenitude. With shared Kripke Dia substituted for primitive Possible, the same collective premise fails in a two-world alternating-witness model, despite reflexivity, finite rigid roster and actual concrete existence. Necessary exemplification does not imply a fixed necessary individual. Separate existence/concrete predicates require a bridge, refuted without it by an explicit nonempty model. No source reading or necessity premise is established; stronger concreteness criteria, source defenses, and actualist/counterpart alternatives remain #435 work. See docs/necessary-individual-quantifiers.md.
